summary: Refunds that time out at the payment gateway are now sent again, up to three attempts in all, waiting 500 ms and then 1 s in between. Any other error, and a timeout on the last attempt, reaches the caller as before. The attempt count and the wait are constants in a new config file.

claims.text: Refund requests that time out at the gateway are tried up to three times.
claims.evidence: The new test "gives up after three attempts" passes on head: five timeouts in a row make three posts, then the timeout is thrown.

claims.text: Nothing changes for a refund that succeeds first time.
claims.evidence: The existing test "sends the refund" passes on base and head with one post.
Two new tests. Both pass on head and fail on base. Neither covers a timeout after the gateway already took the refund.

claims.text: A retried refund is sent again with nothing that lets the gateway tell it is the same refund.
claims.evidence: gateway.post is called with the same body and no idempotency key on every attempt (src/refunds/client.ts:13).

sections.title: The retry loop around the gateway call
sections.why: It changes what reaches the payment gateway when a refund times out.

sections.title: Tests for the retry
sections.why: Two new tests for the new behaviour.
sections.proof: Both pass on head and fail on base; the old test passes on both.

sections.title: Two new constants
sections.why: The attempt count and the wait, used only by the retry loop.
sections.proof: Imported only by client.ts. The values match the description.

decisions.title: A retry sends the same refund again with no idempotency key, so a timeout after the gateway took the refund pays it out twice.
decisions.headline: One refund, paid twice.
decisions.detail: A gateway timeout does not mean the refund failed: the gateway may have made it and only the reply was lost. The retry posts the same body with nothing the gateway can dedupe on. The gateway takes an idempotency key for exactly this (docs/gateway.md:88).
decisions.question: Fix it before anyone reviews it?

options.label: Send an idempotency key
options.detail: Derive it from the refund id, so every attempt of one refund carries the same key.
options.comment: In `RefundClient.refund`, pass `{ idempotencyKey: `refund-${req.id}` }` to `gateway.post` on every attempt, so the gateway dedupes retries of one refund.

options.label: Leave it, and tell reviewers why
options.detail: If the gateway already dedupes by refund id on its side.
options.comment: Retries resend the same refund id, and the gateway dedupes refunds by id, so a retried timeout cannot pay out twice.

options.label: Fine as it is
options.detail: Accept a double refund when a reply is lost.

evidence.title: The gateway takes the refund, then the reply times out

beforeAfter.title: What the customer gets
beforeAfter.scenario: A 5 EUR refund whose first reply times out after the gateway made it.

rows.label: A refund that succeeds first time

decisions.title: A console.log left in the retry loop prints every refund request, with the card's last four digits and the customer's email, to the service log.
decisions.headline: A debug log ships.
decisions.detail: Line 11 logs the whole request on every attempt. A request carries card.last4 and the customer's email (src/refunds/types.ts:6). Nothing else in src/ uses console.log: the service logs through logger, which redacts those fields (src/log.ts:12).
decisions.question: Take it out before review?

options.label: Remove it
options.detail: Log the attempt through logger with the refund id only, or not at all.
options.comment: Remove the `console.log("refund attempt", attempt, req)` line from `RefundClient.refund`.

options.label: Keep it for now, and say why
options.comment: The attempt log is there while we watch the rollout. It goes in the follow-up.

evidence.output: src/refunds/types.ts:6  card: { last4: string; brand: string }; customerEmail: string
